subject: Axis AI — request for temporary uptime policy amendment and remedy cap
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Axis AI — initial ask: temporary uptime policy amendment and remedy cap

Team — forwarding Axis's formal request (attached) and the commercial ask from procurement. Key points: they want a guaranteed 99.5% monthly uptime SLA (we currently publish 99.9%), with a maximum combined service-credit cap of 5% of monthly fees and an explicit allowance for model-fallback routing that can affect P99 latency guarantees. In exchange Axis is committing to a 12-month reserved capacity contract at a materially discounted rate (see attached).

Proposed internal questions I want answered before we engage execs:
- Does Deal Desk have a precedent for a 5% cap (we typically do 10% at minimum)?
- Legal: are we comfortable with explicit fallback language that could allow model-varianting as "operational mitigation"?
- RevOps/Finance: what is the net revenue impact for the discount + reserved commit?

Attachments: Axis_SLA_Request_20270510.pdf; Axis_COMMIT_Proposal.xlsx

Please review — if you think this requires an executive exception, mark the fields that we need to surface in a one-pager for signoff (duration, cap, reporting obligations, telemetry access).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Axis AI — initial ask: temporary uptime policy amendment and remedy cap

Thanks Neha — reviewed the attachments. Short summary and my recommendation:

Summary of Axis ask:
- Monthly uptime: 99.5% (vs our standard 99.9%)
- Remedy: capped service credits at 5% of monthly fees
- Latency: P95 guaranteed; P99 subject to model-fallback/varianting with max tail 500ms
- Commercial: 12-mo reserved commit with ~30% discount on hosted rates

Deal Desk assessment:
- Commercially reasonable to trade a tighter price for a slight SLO concession if we tighten reporting/guardrails.
- We do not typically accept a 5% cap without additional mitigations — propose a tiered credit schedule and a sunset date (90 days pilot, then re-evaluate).

Recommended counter (to present to execs for signoff):
1) Temporary SLO amendment: 99.5% for first 3 months post-go-live (pilot), revert to 99.9% thereafter.
2) Remedy cap: 7.5% of monthly fees during pilot (caps include all credits), then standard remedy schedule after pilot.
3) Mandatory weekly SLO reporting during pilot + realtime alerting integration (Axis must onboard to our telemetry collector).
4) Explicitly allow model-fallback routing only if we provide an alternative model variant with equivalent security controls; fallback cannot be used to permanently reduce latency obligations.
5) Commercial concession: 25% discount for the 12-mo commit (not 30%) to preserve margin.

If you want exec approval for a one-time exception to our SLA policy, I can prepare a one-pager for sign-off. Need confirmation on the revenue impact from Rishi and any legal redlines from Lauren.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Deal Desk
Redwood Inference
From: Jared Cole <jared@axisai.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena@axisai.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Axis AI — initial ask: temporary uptime policy amendment and remedy cap

Neha / Marissa — thank you for the quick read. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- The 99.5% ask is intended to reflect real production behavior for our initial region (we plan multi-region later).
- The 5% cap is to limit exposure to procurement (they must sign off internally for any commercial credits exceeding budget).
- We are fine with a pilot window; we need procurement-signed terms by May 20 to meet our board approval timeline.

We appreciate flexibility on pricing if we can lock the commit by May 20. Happy to jump on a short call if that helps speed approvals.

Best,
Jared
VP of Engineering
Axis AI
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Axis AI — initial ask: temporary uptime policy amendment and remedy cap

Looping in to provide senior review. I support proceeding with a targeted executive exception provided the following are agreed and documented in the counterparty paperwork: 

1) Timebox the SLO amendment to a 90-day pilot with automatic reversion unless both parties agree in writing.
2) Cap for pilot at 7.5% (as Marissa suggested) — this is a commercial guardrail and keeps us aligned to cost expectations.
3) Axis must enable our telemetry and connect alerting within 14 days of go-live; failure to do so voids the pilot SLO.
4) Require trimestral executive business review clause (EBR) for the length of the 12-mo term.

If Legal (Lauren) signs off on the fallback language for model-varianting (must be temporary and disclosed), I will endorse the counter to the execs for final sign-off. Neha — can you secure a DocuSign-ready acceptance of the commercial terms by EOD 2027-05-12? Jared indicated procurement needs signatures by May 20.

- Sean
Sean Gallagher
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared@axisai.com>, Elena Rossi <elena@axisai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Axis AI — executive endorsement for temporary SLO amendment (next steps)

Jared / Elena — thanks for the prompt turnaround and for confirming timelines. Per internal review, Redwood can grant a timeboxed executive exception under the terms below:

Executive-endorsed summary (pilot terms) — approved for signature
- SLO: 99.5% monthly uptime for first 90 days after go-live; reverts to 99.9% thereafter unless mutually extended in writing.
- Remedy: Pilot cap of 7.5% of monthly fees (all service credits combined). Post-pilot, standard remedy schedule applies.
- Latency: P95 guarantee stands. P99 may be subject to model-fallback routing during pilot with an upper bound of 500ms for tail latency when fallback occurs; fallback must be disclosed in routing logs.
- Operational requirements: Axis to onboard to Redwood telemetry collector and enable alerting within 14 days of go-live; weekly SLO reports required during pilot.
- Commercial: 12-month reserved commit at 25% discount, subject to usual payment and termination terms.
- Governance: Quarterly EBRs for the life of the contract.

Attached: redwood_counter_remedy_v1.pdf (counter with explicit clause language). Please review and confirm by EOD May 14 so we can finalize a DocuSign envelope for signature. If Axis can sign by May 20 we will honor the committed pricing.

Attachment stubs: redwood_counter_remedy_v1.pdf (legal counter), DocuSign envelope creation pending.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Neha Kapoor
